assessment.nobel_worthiness: Elucidation of GLP-1 as an incretin and the peptide's translation into therapies that have transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity treatment. Clear, original physiology with exceptional and measurable lasting impact on medicine.
assessment.attribution: Drucker (GLP-1 biology, proglucagon processing, GLP-2), Holst (incretin physiology, GLP-1 secretion and action in humans) and Mojsov (identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) form and early synthesis) form a plausible trio. Knudsen's liraglutide/semaglutide work is largely industrial drug development and is the main alternative or additional claim; Habener and others are not credited in the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Mature: decades of replicated physiology and large outcome trials confirming cardiometabolic benefits. Recognition is timely given the clinical scale.
uncertainties: Priority and credit among Mojsov, Habener and others in the original GLP-1 characterisation is contested and I cannot verify the details independently.
Whether the committee prefers basic physiology over drug development (Knudsen) is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineering patient T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new therapeutic modality. Originality lies in the concept and costimulatory design; impact on haematologic cancer is clear.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain contributed early CAR design with CD28 costimulation, June the clinical translation (4-1BB CARs, first CLL patients). Rosenberg's adoptive cell therapy and early CAR trials are important but arguably a distinct line; Eshhar's original chimeric receptor concept is not in the credited list, which complicates fairness.
assessment.maturity: Approved products and multi-year remissions provide strong clinical confirmation; long-term safety and solid tumour limits are still being defined.
uncertainties: Absence of Zelig Eshhar from the credited names weakens a complete attribution.
Rosenberg's contribution may need separate treatment or inclusion.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Splice-modulating antisense oligonucleotide (nusinersen) that corrects SMN2 exon 7 splicing, turning a fatal infant neuromuscular disease into a treatable one. A clean path from mechanism to cure-like clinical benefit that validated antisense therapy for neurological disease.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing mechanism and ISS-N1 type targeting logic with Bennett's chemistry and development at Ibis/Ionis; the pair is a coherent allocation. Others who identified the ISS-N1 target (Singh/Singh) and SMN gene discovery (Melki, Lefebvre) are outside the credited set.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with ten years of clinical follow-up; independent confirmation from other SMN-targeted modalities supports the approach. Timely but somewhat young.
uncertainties: Whether prior SMN1 gene discovery should be recognised alongside the therapeutic step.
Partial overlap in credit with other antisense pioneers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical and other cancers, with population-level reductions in cervical precancer already documented. The idea of self-assembling L1 VLPs is original and the impact on cancer prevention is large.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (NCI) developed L1 VLPs; Frazer and Zhou (Queensland) independently developed the VLP technology. Zhou Jian died in 1999, which fits the three-person rule only with Lowy, Schiller and Frazer. Parallel work at Georgetown and Merck/GSK adds some allocation uncertainty.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature: more than fifteen years of real-world effectiveness data. The 2008 prize recognised the causal link of HPV and cancer, not the vaccine, so this is a distinct achievement.
uncertainties: Competing priority claims for VLP formation and the posthumous role of Jian Zhou.
Prior recognition of the HPV-cancer connection may reduce perceived novelty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and the proof that inhibiting BCR-ABL kinase can control chronic myeloid leukaemia established the paradigm of targeted cancer therapy. Landmark importance with clear lasting impact; resistance mechanisms (Sawyers) guided later drug generations.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (drug discovery), Druker (clinical proof) and Sawyers (resistance and second-line therapy) form a natural trio, similar to the Lasker award grouping. Janet Rowley, Nowell, Hungerford and Witte (earlier cancer genetic discoveries) are outside this candidate.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: two decades of survival data. The challenge is that recognition has been long awaited, so competitive framing is about relative stature rather than maturity.
uncertainties: Possible reluctance to reward a drug development story rather than an underlying discovery.
Contribution by chemist Jürg Zimmermann is not credited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Light-gated ion channels let investigators control genetically defined neurons with millisecond precision, an enabling method that reshaped neuroscience. The discovery of channelrhodopsins and their use in neurons are both original and widely adopted.
assessment.attribution: Crowded credit: Nagel and Hegemann identified channelrhodopsin function, Bamberg contributed key biophysics, Boyden and Deisseroth demonstrated neuronal control, and Miesenböck made an earlier related approach. A three-person prize cannot fairly cover all.
assessment.maturity: Technique is thoroughly confirmed and ubiquitous in research, but therapeutic impact (e.g. vision restoration) is just emerging, so the case rests on a research tool.
uncertainties: Allocation among six credited people is a serious unresolved issue.
Tool-versus-discovery judgement for a prize in physiology or medicine.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of TOR as the target of rapamycin and its role as a central controller of cell growth and metabolism, with implications for cancer, ageing and immunosuppression. Fundamental and broadly influential concept in cell physiology.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified TOR genetically in yeast and defined it as a growth regulator; Schreiber's chemical genetic work identified the mammalian target of FKBP-rapamycin. Sabatini's mTOR work is substantial but his standing is complicated; Heitman and Hall's early yeast work is intertwined with Schreiber's.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed across species, though clinical translation beyond rapalogs for transplant and certain cancers is limited.
uncertainties: Dispute and complexity over credit between Hall, Heitman, Schreiber, Sabatini and Sabers/Brown.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 as a regulator of cell survival defined a new class of oncogene and the control of apoptosis, culminating in BH3-mimetic drugs such as venetoclax. Original, coherent mechanism with clear therapeutic outcome.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams drove the BCL-2 family work and the mouse models showing survival function; Vaux and Strasser were central collaborators; Korsmeyer, Tsujimoto and Cleary (original t(14;18) cloning) are outside the credited names, so priority is not fully captured.
assessment.maturity: Mature: basic biology confirmed over three decades and clinical efficacy shown in CLL and AML. Apoptosis was recognised in 2002 which may limit novelty perceptions.
uncertainties: Missing credited names for the t(14;18) discovery (Tsujimoto, Cleary).
